text:
sara: Heads up — Zenith POC blocked: they keep getting 401 Invalid API key when calling our embeddings endpoint. We gave them sk-zenith-demo-01 and they attach X-Redwood-Project: zenith-eval.

devon: 401 = key unknown/disabled/region mismatch. Ask for the exact curl + which host their DNS resolves to.

sara: They shared this (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-zenith-demo-01\" \\\
  -H \"X-Redwood-Project: zenith-eval\" \\\
  -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'
```
Response: {\"error\":\"Invalid API key\",\"code\":401}

kai: Also check if their infra rewrites hostname to a regional endpoint. We saw that pattern cause a key to be looked up in the wrong region.

infra-bot: log: [2026-06-02T11:42:00Z] key=sk-zenith-demo-01 action=auth-check result=not-found region=ap-northeast-1

devon: infra-bot shows the key exists in eu-west-1 but request hit ap-northeast-1. If the key is region-scoped, it won't authorize. Two quick fixes: 1) ask them to point to the region where the key exists or 2) create a temp presales key in the region they call.

sara: Customer admin confirms their corporate edge pins outbound traffic to ap-northeast-1 for latency. They can't change it easily.

devon: I'll generate a temp presales key bound to project zenith-eval in ap-northeast-1 and mark it short-lived. Admin-only command (internal):
```bash
redwoodctl keys create --org zenith --project zenith-eval --region ap-northeast-1 --scopes embeddings --ttl 6h --label \"zenith presales temp\"
```

infra-bot: log: [2026-06-02T11:44:30Z] key=sk-zenith-temp-b7 created owner=devon region=ap-northeast-1 bound_projects=[\"zenith-eval\"] ttl=6h

sara: Sent key via secure DM. Customer retried and returns 200 with embeddings. Great.

kai: Couple of follow-ups for the deal: 1) they asked about sustained embeddings throughput — ~200k calls/day expected; capture TPS and suggest volume pricing or Dedicated trial. 2) security question: how to programmatically rotate/revoke keys and whether we support KMS-backed keys.

devon: For presales: programmatic revoke uses control plane DELETE (admin token): `DELETE https://control.redwood.ai/v1/keys/{key_id}`. Production customers can rotate via the UI or the same API with service credentials; we support integrating with customer KMS for CMK in Private deployments. Example (no creds):
```bash
curl -X DELETE https://control.redwood.ai/v1/keys/sk-zenith-temp-b7 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>\"
```

sara: Action items: - revoke old sk-zenith-demo-01 and rotate - add region note to presales sample repo and show `--region` flag - kai to capture throughput numbers for pricing addendum - add the revoke snippet to the security QA response.

devon: I'll revoke the old demo key and post the revoke audit log to the deal thread.

infra-bot: log: [2026-06-02T11:50:10Z] key=sk-zenith-demo-01 action=update state=revoked actor=devon

sara: Customer back to testing. Closing this thread.
